end.summary:
Practised speed = distance ÷ time using a cheetah example.
Practised acceleration a = (v − u)/t, including negative acceleration.
Diya correctly calculated −5 m/s² for braking and −2 m/s² for a velocity change from 20 to 10 m/s.
Discussed that acceleration describes change in velocity and that the sign indicates direction.
Calculated average speed for a return journey as 40 km/h; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: They used the acceleration formula correctly in both recorded attempts and later explained that acceleration describes a change in velocity, while the negative sign shows direction. There was an early mix-up that acceleration only means speeding up; this was corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Diya to explain one braking example and draw velocity and acceleration arrows on a number line.
